title: Adaptive microcoalescer for asymmetrical prompt/response distributions
creator: Marco Li
description: Design and implement an adaptive microbatch coalescer that reduces KV-residency fragmentation and GPU memory pressure for workloads with highly asymmetric prompt and response length distributions (short prompts + long responses, and mixed-turn dialogues). The goal is to preserve tail latency SLOs while lowering tokens-per-second cost and KV eviction churn.
technical_design: We will introduce a lightweight microcoalescer layer inside the existing continuous batching scheduler. The coalescer will observe per-request length estimates (prompt + predicted continuation range) and current KV-residency heatmaps to decide two actions: (1) fuse adjacent short requests into microbatches up to a configurable token budget to increase packing efficiency, and (2) opportunistically delay non-critical long-response continuations for a bounded window to allow hot KV frames to persist. The coalescer uses a runtime hotness score computed from recent KV hits, per-slot residency time, and GPU slab utilization. It will expose knobs for max_microbatch_tokens, delay_budget_ms, hotness_threshold, and a priority override for latency-sensitive routes.
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Spike completed to simulate asymmetric workloads in local runtime; gathered baseline metrics for KV hit-rate and GPU slab fragmentation.
2026-02-25: Prototype microcoalescer integrated with scheduler in emulation mode; synthetic tests show 12% reduction in KV evictions at 95th percentile latency unchanged.
2026-03-03: Implemented hotness score and token-budget enforcement; added telemetry hooks for per-slot residency and microbatch composition breakdowns.
2026-03-09: Internal perf review with infra and runtime teams. Decision to cap delay_budget_ms at 25ms for P99-sensitive routes. Added feature flag gating and per-customer opt-in.

2026-03-11: Running canary in staging across dedicated pool with 10% traffic for long-response workload; initial telemetry indicates 18% lower per-token GPU memory churn and small increase (+1.6ms) in mean latency for delayed continuations.
decisions: Use token-budget-first packing instead of time-window packing to limit tail latency impact for short prompts.
Expose per-route controls: microbatching_enabled, max_microbatch_tokens, delay_budget_ms, and latency_priority to let Console map SLAs to coalescer behavior.
Gate rollout behind feature flag and per-customer opt-in for Dedicated/Private until we have 3 days of stable telemetry in staging.
Metrics required: KV_evictions/sec, KV_hit_rate_1m, GPU_slab_fragmentation_index, microbatch_size_distribution, P95/P99 latency by route.
risks: Delaying continuations could increase user-perceived latency for interactive flows if misconfigured.
Aggressive microcoalescing may increase GPU peak memory if long responses are coalesced incorrectly, raising OOM risk on narrow slabs.
Incorrect hotness scoring could starve cold yet latency-critical requests; requires conservative defaults and per-route overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Staging canary shows >=10% reduction in KV_evictions/sec for mixed-length workloads without degrading P99 latency by more than 5% on routes not marked latency_priority.
No increase in OOM incidents during 72-hour canary across dedicated pools (same traffic mix).
Feature flag enabled with Console controls; per-route telemetry surfaces microbatch and delay metrics for operators.
Automated unit and integration tests for microbatch packing invariants and delay budget enforcement exist in repo.
testing_plan: Unit tests: packing algorithm invariants, hotness score boundaries, and priority overrides.
Integration tests: end-to-end request flows with simulated KV warm/cold cycles and enforced GPU slab quotas.
Load tests: replay of real production traces for 48 hours in staging with microcoalescer on/off toggles to compare metrics.
Chaos testing: inject KV eviction spikes and random long-response surges to validate fallback and safety caps.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; enable for internal infra tests.
2) Enable 5% canary on staging dedicated pool for non-latency routes (72h). Monitor key metrics.
3) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% on staging if stable for 7 days.
4) Pilot with one small Dedicated customer (opt-in) for 7 days.
5) Full Dedicated rollout controlled via Console release toggle; default microcoalescer_off for Hosted until validated.
notes: Follow-up work expected: adaptive quantization-aware packing, integration with Optimize suggestions engine, and a Console UX surface showing microbatch composition per route. Coordinate with Solutions team before enabling for enterprise customers.
